walkthroughs.body_html:
Urban Environments — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Urban Environments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Urban Environments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which African region suffers severe desertification?
options: Sahel
Maghreb
Cape
Horn of Africa

mcqs.q: What is the maximum rainfall in hot deserts?
options: 100mm
250mm
500mm

mcqs.q: Why do informal settlements develop in rapidly growing LIC cities?
options: Rural-urban migration outpaces formal housing supply; migrants build their own homes on marginal land without secure land tenure — driven by housing shortage, not by personal choice.
People live in slums because they prefer them or are too lazy to find better housing.
Informal settlements are built by the government for new migrants.
Mitigation is done by HICs and adaptation is done by LICs.

mcqs.q: Why do people move from rural to urban areas in LICs?
options: Because the government forces them to move to cities.
Because cities in poor countries are always better than the countryside.
Informal settlements are built by the government for new migrants.
A combination of push factors (rural poverty, lack of services, agricultural change) and pull factors (perceived jobs, education, healthcare) — though reality often disappoints.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mitigation and adaptation to climate change?
options: Because the government forces them to move to cities.
Mitigation reduces the causes (cutting greenhouse gas emissions); adaptation reduces the impacts (e.g. building sea walls, drought-resistant crops, early warning systems).
Mitigation and adaptation mean the same thing — both are about stopping climate change.
Mitigation is done by HICs and adaptation is done by LICs.
